_comment: Conditions and pricing on realistic trades. Both work on EVERY trade type - they are extra fields, not types of their own. Timing matters: conditions are evaluated once, when the offer is generated as the villager levels up. Location conditions (biome, dimension, job_site_block, config_flag) are stable for a settled villager and therefore reliable. World-state conditions (weather, day_night, moon_phase, gamerule) are a snapshot of that moment - a trade gated on 'night' stays available in daylight once it has been rolled.

novice._comment: Default logic is AND: both must hold. 'biome' takes either a 'tag' string for a biome tag, or a 'biomes' ARRAY of exact biome ids.
"logic": "or" flips the block to 'any of these'.

apprentice._comment: config_flag reads a boolean from the VillagersPlus config, gamerule reads a world gamerule. Both let a datapack react to how the server is set up.

journeyman._comment: Pricing. price_multiplier is vanilla's per-trade discount weight (how strongly reputation and Hero of the Village move the price). demand seeds vanilla's demand tracking: the price rises with use and decays over time. Both are scaled globally by trade_price_multiplier_scale and trade_cost_scale in the config; reputation and Hero of the Village discounts are applied by vanilla on top.

job_site_block gates on the block the villager is employed at. Give it a 'blocks' ARRAY of block ids, or a 'wood_variant' string that is matched against the block id's path - that is how the flower tub's twelve wood types are told apart.
